classification.difficultyReason: Differentiate and check the velocity sign around its zero, then use the established reversal to split the distance travelled and connect the velocity and displacement to the motion description and cubic sketch.

content.prompt:
A particle moves so that its displacement is given by

$$x=t^3-3t$$

where $x$ is in metres and $t$ is time in seconds.

children.label: a
children.prompt: In what direction is the particle moving initially?

answer.worked: Differentiating $x=t^3-3t$ gives $v(t)=3t^2-3$. Since $v(0)=-3\,\mathrm{m/s}$, the particle initially moves left.

children.label: b
children.prompt: When does the particle first come to rest?

answer.worked:
At rest, $v(t)=0$.

$$\begin{align*}3t^2-3&=0\\t^2&=1\\t&=\pm1\end{align*}$$

Since $t\geq0$, the particle first comes to rest at $t=1$ second.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Determine whether the particle changes direction at this time.

answer.worked: For $0\leq t<1$, $v(t)=3(t^2-1)<0$. For $t>1$, $v(t)>0$. The velocity changes sign at $t=1$, so the particle changes direction from left to right.

children.label: d
children.prompt: When and where does the particle change direction?

answer.worked: The velocity changes sign at $t=1$ second. The displacement then is $x(1)=1^3-3(1)=-2\,\mathrm{m}$, so the particle turns 2 metres to the left of its starting point.

children.label: e
children.prompt: Find the distance travelled in the first 3 seconds.

answer.worked:
The particle turns at $t=1$. Its displacements at the start, the turn and the end of the interval are $x(0)=0$, $x(1)=-2$ and $x(3)=3^3-3(3)=18$ metres. Add the distances on either side of the turn.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Distance}&=|-2-0|+|18-(-2)|\\\text{Distance}&=2+20\\\text{Distance}&=22\,\mathrm{m}\end{align*}$$

children.label: f
children.prompt: Describe the motion of the particle.

answer.short: It starts at the origin, moves left while slowing, stops at $t=1$ second at $x=-2\,\mathrm{m}$, then moves right with increasing speed. It passes the origin again at $t=\sqrt{3}$ seconds.
answer.worked: The particle starts at $x(0)=0$ with $v(0)=-3\,\mathrm{m/s}$. Its velocity $v(t)=3t^2-3$ increases for $t\geq0$. The speed decreases while the velocity is negative. At $t=1$ second the particle stops at $x=-2\,\mathrm{m}$ and reverses. From then on, the positive velocity increases, so the particle speeds up to the right. Since $x(t)=t(t^2-3)$, it passes the origin again at $t=\sqrt{3}$ seconds.

children.label: g
children.prompt: Draw the displacement–time graph of the particle.

answer.short: The graph starts at $(0,0)$, turns at $(1,-2)$ and crosses the time axis again at $(\sqrt{3},0)$.
answer.worked: Use $t\geq0$. The displacement $x(t)=t(t^2-3)$ is zero at $t=0$ and $t=\sqrt{3}$. The gradient $3t^2-3$ is negative for $0\leq t<1$, zero at $t=1$ and positive for $t>1$. Draw the curve down from $(0,0)$ to its minimum at $(1,-2)$, then up through $(\sqrt{3},0)$. The curve is concave up for $t>0$ because $x''(t)=6t>0$.

spec.sourceRegion: Answer book, printed page 356, Exercise 7L Q8(g)

spec.mathematics: Plot x=t³−3t for t≥0. The visible landmarks are the origin, the minimum (1,−2) and the positive intercept at t=√3. Both grid steps are 1 in the corresponding coordinate units.
